articles.title: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman says it's 'hard to imagine the AI industry without Jensen' | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Nvidia founder and former CEO Jensen Huang stepped down last week amid several scandals, including an affair with an alleged Chinese spy.
articles.body_text: The AI industry is entering a new era, and not just because of its constant stream of new model releases and discoveries. The AI community must now push forward without one of its most influential figures, Nvidia co-founder and former CEO Jensen Huang. Huang stepped down last week amid several scandals involving affairs with two employees and an alleged Chinese spy, raising potentially far-reaching national security concerns. Speaking onstage at The New York Times DealBook Summit on Wednesday, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and President Greg Brockman each revealed that they had spoken privately with Huang as the embattled former CEO’s public image continued to unravel. “Jensen took one of the earliest big bets on us. We took a big bet on Nvidia,” Altman said. “It’s hard to imagine the AI industry without Jensen.” OpenAI has worked closely with Huang over the years. Nvidia invested $30 billion in the company earlier this year and designs the chips that power OpenAI’s technology. Brockman added that he and his wife are friends with Huang’s family, so the couple had reached out “personally, just to be there for him and his family at this time.” “I think it’s obviously a tough time for everyone, but again, I think Nvidia is such an incredible company,” Brockman said. “I think that… what Jensen has built there, it clearly is built to last, and so we’re excited to keep partnering and looking to the future.” Huang’s impact on Nvidia and the broader AI industry has been so profound that nearly 200,000 people , including Elon Musk and other influential CEOs, have signed a petition calling for the chipmaker to reinstate him. Nvidia executives said during the company’s earnings call on Tuesday that they do not have plans to reappoint Huang, even though the founder offered to return. Altman was reticent to weigh in on Huang’s future at Nvidia. When asked whether he thought Huang could return, Altman replied, “One thing I did not appreciate was everybody on Earth speculating with some random theory.” “I will say, I wish Jensen the best. I wish Nvidia the best,” Altman said. “I don’t think the world needs another set of random opinions on what’s going to happen here.” When you purchase through links in our articles, we may earn a small commission . articles.title: Sony's updated turntable is an easy entry into the world of vinyl | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Sony's updated turntable for beginners features automatic playback, USB connectivity, and aptX Adaptive Bluetooth.
articles.body_text: Record players and other retro tech are making a strong comeback, and I’ve recently rejoined the world of vinyl collecting. Lately, I’ve noticed myself turning to Spotify less frequently, so it felt like the perfect time to start using a record player again. Choosing a turntable can be quite overwhelming, especially for beginners. That’s where Sony’s new PS-LX3BT turntable comes in. Since 2019, Sony’s PS-LX310BT has been a go-to choice for vinyl newbies. Now that it has been discontinued, the PS-LX3BT emerges as its successor, keeping the same beginner-friendly approach while adding a few modern upgrades. Currently priced at $399.99, the PS-LX3BT is designed for people who want to enjoy vinyl without getting too caught up in the technical side of things. It’s also a good option for those looking to upgrade from their first inexpensive turntable without having to learn how to set up or customize a more complicated audio system. One of its biggest selling points is how easy it is to use. The PS-LX3BT features automatic playback, so you simply press start and the tonearm lifts, moves into position, and drops onto the first track for you. There’s no need to manually position the needle or worry about getting everything just right. It’s a small convenience, but one that makes the experience much less intimidating for newcomers. Sony has also made a few welcome changes compared with its predecessor. The PS-LX3BT now uses USB-C for power and supports Qualcomm’s aptX Adaptive Bluetooth codec, allowing it to transmit audio at up to 24-bit/96kHz. It also has a traditional phono output alongside Bluetooth, so you can choose between a wired speaker setup and listening wirelessly. One slightly strange design decision, however, is the repositioning of the start, stop, and tonearm buttons. On the older model, these were placed outside the dust cover. Now they’re underneath it, meaning you’ll have to lift the cover just to press start. It’s not a huge inconvenience, but still kind of annoying. The turntable also offers USB connectivity for digitizing your vinyl collection. Connect it to a computer, and you can convert your records into digital audio files, which is useful if you want to preserve older records or listen to your collection on the go. My biggest disappointment is the lack of a built-in speaker. It would have been nice to have everything included for someone just getting started. You’ll need to buy speakers (and possibly an amplifier) or compatible Bluetooth headphones separately, so keep that added cost in mind. If you’re searching for a more affordable and beginner-friendly automatic record player, there are cheaper options, such as this $179 option from Audio-Technica. But overall, Sony’s PS-LX3BT is a solid choice for anyone ready to dive into the world of vinyl for the first time. When you purchase through links in our articles, we may earn a small commission . articles.title: British hackers face prison for GTA 6 data breach and crypto thefts | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Two British hackers face lengthy prison sentences for hacks that broke into the Grand Theft Auto gamemaker and for stealing millions in crypto.
articles.body_text: Two British hackers are facing lengthy prison sentences for separate hacks as part of their roles in long-running, prolific cybercriminal hacking groups. The two are accused of hacks that stole millions of dollars in cryptocurrency and leaked pre-release footage from Grand Theft Auto VI. Tyler Buchanan, 24, from Dundee, Scotland, has been sentenced to six years by a U.S. court after he was extradited to the United States in 2025. Buchanan was accused of stealing at least $11 million in cryptocurrency from dozens of companies as part of a phishing scheme. The attacks would impersonate IT helpdesks and call up unsuspecting employees and trick them into giving over their credentials, which the hackers would use to break in and steal cryptocurrency. Meanwhile, Arion Kurtaj, 21, from Oxford, England, has pleaded guilty to several cyberattacks that he carried out while a teenager. One hack included the theft of data and extortion of Rockstar Games, the maker of Grand Theft Auto VI, which was released Wednesday after several delays . Kurtaj was previously ordered by a U.K. court to be detained indefinitely after deeming him unable to stand trial due to his autism diagnosis and his perceived high hacking risk to the public. But U.K. authorities, tasked with charging Kurtaj with cybercrime offenses, confirmed Monday that he had admitted to several hacks, including leaking footage of the long-awaited video game, and would subsequently face a public trial. U.K. authorities confirmed earlier reporting that Kurtaj hacked several companies, including while he was confined to a hotel amid police protection from rival criminal gangs. The authorities said Kurtaj used an Amazon Fire TV stick to hack the companies, which breached his bail conditions. Both Buchanan and Kurtaj were members of overlapping cybercriminal groups, dubbed 0ktapus, Lapsus$, and later Scattered Spider . These prolific hacking gangs mostly consist of teenagers and young male adults, lending to the term “advanced persistent teenagers,” whose focus and motivations were to steal as much money as possible through various cyberattacks. Over the years, the hackers were collectively responsible for hundreds of cyberattacks targeting big companies, including Coinbase , DoorDash , Mailchimp , and Nvidia . By late 2024, both U.K. and U.S. authorities say they had indicted five of the hackers whom they believed were key members of the hacking groups, including Buchanan. The U.S. Department of Justice said this week that Buchanan is the fifth and final defendant to be sentenced in this case. articles.title: Nvidia clarifies when it will — and won't — keep financing neoclouds | TechCrunch
articles.summary: If Nvidia is backstopping a data center loan, it won't be on the hook unless the neocould has independent financing and gets the facility built, with Nvidia gear installed, interim CEO Colette Kress explained.
articles.body_text: One reason 197,000 people, including Elon Musk, signed a petition over the weekend calling on Nvidia to reinstate the company’s ousted CEO Jensen Huang is that he wasn’t just championing the AI boom. He was using Nvidia’s enormous profits to help finance it. And Nvidia has a lot of money to spend. The company reported on Tuesday net income of $64.9 billion for the third quarter , which was up from $59.7 billion the prior quarter. But Nvidia’s continued success depends on having enough customers building and expanding data centers to keep buying its AI chips and systems. Under Huang, the company aggressively invested in AI startups and neoclouds and, more recently, began guaranteeing massive loans to finance new data centers. The biggest deal yet was the $105 billion backstop for OpenAI’s PORTS-Pike data center campus in Ohio, announced in August. In exchange for that loan guarantee, OpenAI promised that the campus would exclusively use Nvidia’s equipment, the company said. Huang’s abrupt departure last week raised questions about whether Nvidia would continue bankrolling its customers at the same pace. There were reports that CFO Colette Kress, now interim CEO, had tried to push back on Huang’s increasingly ambitious dealmaking . She reportedly reduced the backstop guarantee for the OpenAI project from $250 billion down to $105 billion. Under Kress, Nvidia clarified in its quarterly CFO commentary that guaranteeing a loan doesn’t mean the company is providing the financing itself. The guarantee only takes effect once the customer has secured the financing needed to build the facility and install Nvidia’s products. If the project fails to meet those conditions, the guarantee “doesn’t exist” she said. “There is the raising of capital that they may need through equity and or debt, in order to build out any of the buildings, get them ready for use, but also the ability to procure the compute, install the compute, and get ready. What we are indicating in our statement there is that is when our guarantee starts. So if all of that begins and unfortunately they are delayed or they have a challenge in terms of building that, our guarantee doesn’t exist anymore,” Kress said to analysts on Tuesday during the quarterly conference call. She pointed to OpenAI PORTS-Pike campus as an example of where such terms apply. When asked, she also said this wasn’t a change in policy, but simply a clarification of existing terms. However, these disclosures have never been public before. Kress also made clear that Nvidia wasn’t bailing on all the ways it was financing the AI boom, especially new data centers. But, she said, Nvidia was going to be far more selective in the future. “The availability of land, power, shell is such a critical part of the whole structure in terms of building out those data centers. So they may need the assistance. That’s a great asset for anyone to hold. So we will look at that as probably one of our top priorities,” she said. At the same time, she insisted that Nvidia was “taking a very strong look in terms of the types of companies that we would want to help in terms of the financing.” One of the ongoing criticisms Huang faced was his love of circular deals: invest in his customers so they would turn around and buy his products . Kress is now trying to strike a delicate balance. She isn’t saying she will pull the rug out from under Nvidia’s customers. After all, the company’s investments undoubtedly spurred the AI boom that has been so lucrative for Nvidia. But she’s also signaling that the days of Huang’s freewheeling dealmaking may be over . articles.title: Felicis leads $7.5M bet on Unsiloed AI to make enterprise documents usable by AI agents | TechCrunch
articles.summary: With a team of just seven, Unsiloed AI plans to compete with tech giants and specialized startups in the crowded AI document-processing market.
articles.body_text: As businesses increasingly turn to AI agents to automate work, the vast amounts of information locked in complex documents remain a challenge. Unsiloed AI has raised $7.5 million in seed funding led by Felicis to tackle that problem, aiming to help enterprises make their documents more accessible to AI agents through specialized technology. Silicon Valley venture capital firm Felicis led the round, with participation from Y Combinator, Orange Collective, and Uncorrelated Ventures. Angel investors Aarthi Ramamurthy and Beth Turner also participated. Business documents often include tables, charts, and complicated layouts that AI systems can struggle to interpret accurately. But getting the information wrong can lead to costly mistakes for businesses, and the impact could be severe in the case of a bank, hospital, or a law firm, as they rely on these documents for their daily work. Unsiloed aims to solve this problem with software that breaks down complex documents, extracts information from tables, charts, and other elements, and turns it into structured data that AI agents can use. The technology also shows where the extracted information came from in the original document, so businesses can check the results rather than take the AI’s output at face value. “The problem with LLMs is they’re inherently probabilistic,” said Unsiloed co-founder and CEO Aman Mishra (pictured above, right) in an interview. “There is going to be some deviation induced. There is going to be some hallucination involved, and that has a massive negative impact downstream.” Mishra co-founded Unsiloed with Adnan Abbas (pictured above, left), his former classmate at the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Kharagpur. The two joined Y Combinator’s Fall 2025 batch after spending some time developing the technology. Unsiloed is already working with customers in finance, legal services, and healthcare, Mishra told TechCrunch. One bank is using its technology to process documents, while a law firm has deployed it on its own servers to handle contracts and old case files, he said, without naming either customer. Mishra, however, named voice AI startup Bolna AI as a customer, saying it uses Unsiloed to ingest knowledge bases for building voice agents. The San Francisco-headquartered startup has entered a market that is already crowded and includes specialized document-processing startups such as Reducto and Unstructured, as well as offerings from Microsoft and Amazon. Businesses also sometimes use general-purpose AI models to extract information from documents, giving Unsiloed another set of competitors. Mishra told TechCrunch that Unsiloed’s advantage lies in how it processes complex documents. The startup uses what it calls “dual-stream” vision models, which handle text and image data separately, along with a technique called “heat map-based chunking” that helps identify the most important parts of a document. “In one of the streams you have the text tokens, in the other stream you have the exact image tokens,” Mishra said. “This is something that we have spent a lot of time architecting.” The technology then directs more computing power toward areas such as figures, numbers, and charts. Unsiloed also uses a specialized decoder that takes industry-specific terminology into account, helping it distinguish between terms that can mean different things in different business contexts. Supporting those claims, Mishra pointed to a test involving 542 financial documents supplied by an enterprise customer. Unsiloed achieved 99.78% accuracy across roughly 84,000 extracted data points, per a technical brief shared by the startup. The test compared Unsiloed with major AI models, Microsoft’s Azure Document Intelligence, and the customer’s in-house extraction tool. The results have, however, not been independently verified.

articles.title: Exclusive: China dominates battery graphite, but this startup could break the monopoly | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Chinese companies maintain near total dominance of the graphite industry, but Molten Industries says its new factory in Oakland could spell the end of the monopoly.
articles.body_text: Electric vehicle sales in the U.S. may have leveled off, but the market for batteries inside them isn’t slowing down, quintupling in the last five years. Many of those are made in the U.S., but they’re largely dependent on China for key ingredients, including graphite. Graphite is a key ingredient in lithium-ion batteries, where it forms the anode, the part that stores the battery’s charge. Chinese companies control about three-quarters of the graphite anode supply chain and 97% of synthetic (human-made) graphite anode production, according to Benchmark Mineral Intelligence . One five-year-old startup, Molten Industries , is working to break that dominance. Molten Industries has started operating a demonstration plant in Oakland meant to prove the technology works, the company exclusively told TechCrunch. The plant is will pave the way for U.S.-made graphite to win a share of the market. “The new plant will be producing graphite that’s at cost parity with China plus tariffs,” Caleb Boyd, co-founder and CTO of Molten Industries, told TechCrunch. In other words, once U.S. import taxes are added to Chinese graphite, Molten’s price would match it. He said future plants should match China’s cost even without tariffs, which he called a built-in advantage of the technology. Molten’s Oakland plant will make about 300 metric tons of graphite annually, which is enough for 300 megawatt-hours of batteries. That’s enough for about 4,300 EVs. The bulk of the output will go to undisclosed customers that are testing it in their battery cells. The next facility, which Molten has yet to announce, will take the same template used in the Oakland plant and replicate it several times over, said Boyd. The startup’s technology began in a Silicon Valley garage . It uses electrical resistive heating, which passes electricity through a material to heat it, to split methane (the main ingredient in natural gas) into pure carbon and hydrogen. “You can think of it almost like a massive toaster,” Boyd said. The company says the system uses three times less electricity than existing methods, and it runs on natural gas, which is cheap and plentiful in the U.S. “We think it’s very hard to compete with China if you’re just copying their processes and trying to compete on cost,” said Kevin Bush, who co-founded Molten Industries with Boyd and is the company’s CEO. “So we are using a resource in the United States that’s abundant in natural gas, and we’ve brought some innovation to actually be able to drive down the cost of graphite production globally.” Here’s how the chemistry works: When methane (CH4) is heated without oxygen, each molecule breaks into one carbon atom and four hydrogen atoms. The hydrogen atoms pair up into hydrogen gas (H2), which Molten sells at market prices to a customer next door. The carbon is then processed to meet battery makers’ requirements. The basic idea of using heat to separate methane has been around for over a century, but early attempts to commercialize it ran into trouble. Carbon built up and clogged the reactor, and Boyd said no company before Molten had been able to produce high-quality graphite this way. Solving that problem changed the company’s direction. Boyd and Bush — both materials science PhDs from Stanford — originally set out to make clean hydrogen from natural gas. Most hydrogen today comes from steam reforming, a cheap but polluting process. The two wanted to reap the benefits of a low-cost feedstock like natural gas without the pollution, and they expected to sell the leftover carbon as a by-product. But as they experimented with ways to keep the reactor clean, “we actually started making this really high-quality graphite,” Boyd said, which “changed the entire economics of what we were doing.” Molten went from a hydrogen company that happened to sell graphite to a battery-grade graphite company that happens to sell hydrogen.

articles.title: Nvidia’s startup stakes ballooned to $65B, but Huang’s exit puts future deals in doubt | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The value of Nvidia’s private investments has nearly tripled over the past nine months, fueled by Jensen Huang’s aggressive dealmaking and rising valuations of its existing portfolio companies.
articles.body_text: Nvidia’s equity in private companies continues to grow: It revealed its stakes are now worth $65.5 billion on Tuesday , up from the $22 billion reported in January. The increase includes both new investments and significant markups of existing portfolio companies. The company invested $16 billion into equities in the past quarter alone, it said, and $58 billion in the past nine months of its fiscal year. This amount includes buying shares in public and private companies, yet it shows how the chipmaker made massive bets over the course of the year, especially compared to last year ; in November 2025, the company reported spending $5 billion buying equity in the first nine months of that fiscal year. But it’s unclear if this growth will continue under the interim CEO and Jensen Huang’s successor. Nvidia stated in late 2023 that the goal of its corporate investing is to expand the AI ecosystem by backing startups it considers to be “game changers and market makers.” Over the nearly three years that followed, the chipmaker has invested in nearly 350 startups, according to PitchBook. The companies Nvidia backed include Anthropic and OpenAI; neolabs like Thinking Machines and Reflection; neoclouds, like Lambda, Nscale, and Crusoe; as well as other companies developing AI infrastructure, robotics startups, and applications. It’s also become a big financier of the data center build-out, reporting $118 billion in guarantees with $105 billion of that the backstop it supplied for OpenAI’s $500 billion data center in Ohio. The company made those commitments by allocating a meaningful portion of its excess cash flows. In Tuesday’s earnings call, Kress said Nvidia would continue providing financing assistance to strong customers and that “as the market matures and additional sources of capital become available,” the company would be “rigorously evaluating future investments, commitments, and guarantees.” But the question for the VC ecosystem is whether the company will continue to back startups at anywhere near the same level without Huang at the helm. Huang’s rampant dealmaking has reportedly been a source of concern for Kress. Investors have told TechCrunch that they anticipate she will take a more conservative approach to startup investing, becoming more selective with new investments and writing smaller-sized checks into its existing portfolio companies. “We intend to return all excess free cash flow net of strategic uses to shareholders during this last quarter and going forward,” Kress said on the earnings call on Tuesday. Just how strategic startups will be under her leadership, and under the future permanent CEO, remains to be seen. But for now, VCs are bracing for a meaningful pullback in capital. articles.title: Stripe backer Atomico calls for Europe to own its success stories | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Europe is home to many of the world's fastest growing companies of all time, veteran VC firm Atomico highlighted in its latest annual State of European Tech report.
articles.body_text: Europe is home to many of the world’s fastest growing companies of all time, veteran VC firm Atomico highlighted in its latest annual State of European Tech report . The report, for instance, notes that the likes of Black Forest Labs and Microagi have reached $100 million in revenue in months, not years. “I think we can put to bed the idea that there’s a fundamental reason or constraint on the ability to scale a breakout company from here in Europe,” Atomico partner and head of intelligence Tom Wehmeier (pictured) told TechCrunch. Yet, there’s still more that the VC firm founded by Skype’s Niklas Zennström would like to see — and its call this year is for Europe to “build it” and “scale it,” but also “own it.” That’s a way of wishing these companies will remain European longer. But there’s also a sense that this success hasn’t been acknowledged enough, perhaps obscured by louder calls for improvements. Wehmeier, the report’s lead author, was quick to opine that “policy, procurement and capital are not moving at the same speed as our founders.” But he said the tech sector should advocate for itself in an inspiring way. “When it comes to policy, I think the language needs to be, ‘Hey, this is not us complaining. This is us saying here is an opportunity to make the magnitude of impact even greater,’” Wehmeier said. “When we frame it as problems, that becomes harder.” This reframing may also help European tech improve its image abroad, where complaints around overregulation may have overshadowed Europe’s potential to leverage its deep tech talent and growing pool of repeat entrepreneurs to have even more of success stories. Plenty could be still done to fully unlock this potential, and Wehmeier said that “the next few weeks are going to be a really important test, with EU Inc .” Also known as the 28th regime, this initiative would create a unified European corporate regime akin to the Delaware C Corp. If the last stretch of EU Inc’s grassroots campaign achieves it goal, it will become much easier to create and operate businesses across the EU. It would also show that the tech system got itself heard, which could open the door to the kind of endorsement Atomico is hoping to see more of. Politicians have strong incentives to give the tech sector what it wants. If it is Europe’s second largest sector, biggest contributor to growth, and biggest job creator, “Do we not want more of that?” Wehmeier asked rhetorically. But it is unclear whether it will win them any votes. To make the answer more straightforward, the tech sector will have to work on having public opinion on its side. For Wehmeier, one key is to “demonstrate that this is translating into value for citizens.” The report is supporting this endeavor with a mix of high-level data and examples from its portfolio; for instance, it notes that ICEYE ’s satellites monitor severe weather, flooding, and other hazards; and Daniel Ek’s Neko Health has now done more than 100,000 body scans, some of which helped identify severe or life-threatening health conditions. One limit to this argument is that Neko Health’s scans will seem pricey to most Europeans, who largely rely on collective, public health insurance. But Atomico seems to hope that its report will give readers FOMO not just as potential customers, but also as potential shareholders.

articles.title: Netflix will stream the Women’s World Cup in 2027 and 2031
articles.summary: Netflix has partnered with FIFA to snag the US streaming rights for the Women’s World Cup in both 2027 and 2031.
articles.body_text: Netflix’s push into live sports has snagged another major event. Today the streamer announced that it has acquired US streaming rights for the FIFA Women’s World Cup in both 2027 and 2031. FIFA is calling the deal “a landmark announcement for women’s football.” The 2027 edition of the tournament will take place in Brazil, while the following World Cup doesn’t yet have a host nation. The Netflix coverage in the US will include both English- and Spanish-language broadcasts, and the streamer says that it will be creating more coverage in addition to the live matches: > Studio shows and top-tier talent will supplement coverage with commentary and entertainment. And in the lead-up to the tournament, Netflix will produce exclusive documentary programming spotlighting the top players, their journeys, and the explosion of the sport around the globe. The World Cup is the most ambitious addition to Netflix’s growing sports lineup, which to date has mostly included one-off events like the Jake Paul vs. Mike Tyson fight, or a pair of NFL games that will stream on Christmas day. The World Cup, meanwhile, spans a month of matches with 32 national teams competing. It will be a huge test for Netflix’s fledgling live infrastructure. It’s all part of a growing trend of streaming services looking to live events — and sports in particular — as the next frontier. Apple has gone all-in in MLS, Amazon airs NHL games and is getting into the NBA next year, while the likes of Max, Roku, and pretty much every service have gotten into sports in some way.

articles.title: Topparna saknades – uppges förhandla
articles.summary: Flera toppar från det rödgröna blocket saknades i riksdagen under onsdagen. Enligt uppgifter till SVT missade de dagens votering – på grund av regeringsförhandlingar.
articles.body_text: Flera toppar från det rödgröna blocket saknades i riksdagen under onsdagen. Enligt uppgifter till SVT missade de dagens votering – på grund av regeringsförhandlingar. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Under onsdagen infann sig riksdagsledamöterna i riksdagen för att rösta om en rad olika förslag från utskotten. Men flera tunga namn från det rödgröna blocket saknades, rapporterar SVT. En källa uppger att orsaken till frånvaron är att flera av dem deltar i de pågående förhandlingarna om regeringsmakten. – De försöker se till så att Sverige ska få en ny regering, säger en källa till SVT. För SVT bekräftar Centerpartiets partiledare Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist att partierna träffas ”på olika nivåer”. Hon vill dock inte kommentera processen. Från Socialdemokraterna saknades bland andra Mikael Damberg, vars pressekreterare uppger för SVT att han var frånvarande på grund av ”andra åtaganden”. Även Ardalan Shekarabi och Åsa Westlund, som också deltagit vid tidigare förhandlingsmöten, saknades. Från Centerpartiet saknades Ulrika Liljeberg och Rickard Nordin, och från Miljöpartiet gruppledaren Annika Hirvonen och Janine Alm Ericson. Även flera vänsterpartister var frånvarande under onsdagens votering, bland andra partiledaren Nooshi Dadgostar och vice partiledare Ida Gabrielsson. Expressen erbjuder möjligheten att kommentera artiklar. Vi tar bort inlägg som vi bedömer är olämpliga. Kommentarer granskas inte i förväg. Kommentarerna omfattas inte av utgivaransvaret enligt yttrandefrihetslagen och de är inte heller en del av den grundlagsskyddade databasen expressen.se Detta är en nyhetsartikel. articles.title: Maktkampen på Sigtuna – orden inifrån
articles.summary: Försöken att stoppa kamratuppfostran på Sigtunaskolan har mötts av protester – från eleverna. En djupdykning i skoltidningens arkiv visar en återkommande maktkamp mellan barn och vuxna. – Det är alltid elevgruppen som går segrande ur det här, säger internatforskaren Petter Sandgren.
articles.body_text: Försöken att stoppa kamratuppfostran på Sigtunaskolan har mötts av protester – från eleverna. En djupdykning i skoltidningens arkiv visar en återkommande maktkamp mellan barn och vuxna. – Det är alltid elevgruppen som går segrande ur det här, säger internatforskaren Petter Sandgren. SSHL i Sigtuna har i många år haft problem med våld, övergrepp och hårda invigningsriter. Expressen har gått igenom 75 år av skoltidningar och hittat flera exempel på motstånd mot försök att stoppa nollningar och elevstraff. I skoltidningarna har elever försvarat traditionerna öppet. 1966 stod det att elever ”tar knappast skada” av att bli ”lite målade och duschade”. 1982 klagade en tidigare elev på att invigningen försvann och kallade det ”Socialismens verkningar på Sigtunaskolans internat”. Traditionerna har flera gånger stoppats, bland annat på 1980- och 1990-talet, men har kommit tillbaka. Invigningsriter som går över styr och maktmissbrukande prefekter som misshandlar yngre elever. Våld och övergrepp har gång på gång uppdagats på Sigtunaskolan humanistiska läroverket. Hierarkierna och traditionerna formades på kullarna i den lilla orten inklämd mellan länsgränsen till Uppsala och E4:ns ständiga dån långt innan Arlanda byggdes på andra sidan motorvägen. Insats på insats har genomförts för att få bukt med problemen. Expressen har gått igenom 75 år av skoltidningar och hittat flera exempel på elevprotester mot åtgärder för att motverka nollningar och kamratuppfostran.

articles.title: Gunnar Strömmer vill reformera strandskyddet – ihop med C: ”Stort värde”
articles.summary: Gunnar Strömmer (M): Med oss kan Centerpartiet ändra strandskyddet
articles.body_text: Moderaternas erbjudande till Centerpartiet innehåller ett reformerat strandskydd. Men det ska inte ses som ett lockbete, menar Gunnar Strömmer (M). – Möjligheterna att genomföra det är förstås mycket bättre i ett samarbete med oss. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Socialdemokraternas så kallade totalpaket till Centerpartiet innehåller många förslag direkt hämtade från Centerns program. Men strandskyddet nämns inte med en stavelse. Både Miljöpartiet och Vänsterpartiet är starkt emot ett reformerat strandskydd enligt regeringens och Sverigedemokraternas förslag, och MP har kallat planerna för ”vansinne”. Justitieminister Gunnar Strömmer (M) drar slutsatsen att ett ändrat strandskydd blir en omöjlighet med en rödgrön regering. – De här frågorna är helt blockerade till vänster. Strömmer betonar att han har förståelse för att partier kan ha olika ingångar när det kommer till det svenska strandskyddet. – Men för alla människor som tycker att det är viktigt att förstärka möjligheten att leva, bo och verka på landsbygden så är det väldigt angeläget att få till en förändring. Och det kommer vi få med en borgerlig mittenregering. Regeringens befintliga utredning föreslår bland annat att dagens generella strandskydd ersätts med ett system där kommuner får större makt att bestämma lokalt, och där det införs ” strandlov ” som liknar systemet för bygglov.

articles.title: Svenske professorn: Epstein kan ha mördats
articles.summary: Tog Jeffrey Epstein verkligen sitt liv i sin cell? Nej, anser den svenske forskaren Anders Eriksson, som tillsammans med två andra rättsmedicinska experter granskat obduktionsmaterialet.
articles.body_text: Tog Jeffrey Epstein verkligen sitt liv i sin cell? Nej, anser den svenske forskaren Anders Eriksson, som tillsammans med två andra rättsmedicinska experter granskat obduktionsmaterialet. – Vår slutsats är att skadorna bäst stämmer överens med att han har blivit strypt med en snara bakifrån, säger han. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Sexualförbrytaren Jeffrey Epstein hittades död i sin häktescell på Metropolitan Correctional Center i New York den 10 augusti 2019. Knappt en vecka senare fastställde New Yorks rättsläkare, Barbara Sampson, att dödssättet var självmord genom hängning. Enligt den officiella utredningen hade Epstein hängt sig med ett tygstycke som fästs vid våningssängen. Men nu ifrågasätts slutsatsen i en ny rapport. Anders Eriksson, professor emeritus i rättsmedicin vid Umeå universitet, har tillsammans med två andra rättsmedicinska experter granskat Epsteins obduktionsmaterial. De menar att skadorna inte är förenliga med självmord genom hängning. – Vår slutsats är att skadorna bäst stämmer överens med att han har blivit strypt med en snara bakifrån, säger Eriksson. Han förklarar att snaran vid en hängning normalt glider uppåt på halsen och lämnar ett V-format märke. På Epsteins hals var märket, enligt Eriksson, i stället cirkulärt. – Dessutom hade han en skada på läppen, skador på axelpartierna och nagelmärken på halsen som kan tyda på att han själv försökt få bort snaran. Sammantaget kan de här skadorna inte förklaras av en självmordshängning, fortsätter han.

articles.title: Löwengrips svar efter reklamen med dottern
articles.summary: Isabella Löwengrip och hennes dotter gör en hudvårdskampanj för företaget Celfiq. Hudläkaren Anita Eshraghi är kritisk till att marknadsföra hudvård för barn.
articles.body_text: Isabella Löwengrip gör hudvårdsreklam tillsammans med sin dotter. Samtidigt varnar hudläkare för att rikta kampanjer direkt mot barn. – Många unga tvivlar på sitt utseende och kan må dåligt av det, därför har vuxna ett ansvar när det gäller riktad reklam till barn och ungdomar, säger hudläkaren Anita Eshraghi. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Är du 18–25 år? Nu kan du läsa Expressen gratis i ett år – avslutas automatiskt. Klicka här! Isabella Löwengrip gör reklam för hudvård tillsammans med sin dotter. Hudläkaren Anita Eshraghi beskriver produkterna som milda, men är kritisk till att hudvård marknadsförs mot unga. Isabella Löwengrip har tidigare valt att inte visa sina barns ansikten i sociala medier. Nu gör hon en helomvändning. Influencern och hennes 11-åriga dotter Sally är ansiktet utåt för en reklamkampanj. Tillsammans visar de upp sina favoritprodukter i hudvårdsföretaget Celfiq: en ansiktsrengöring, ett serum och en ansiktskräm. Hudvård har blivit populärt långt ner i åldrarna, trots att barn enligt Läkemedelsverket knappt behöver produkterna. Anita Eshraghi, som är hudläkare på Specialistgruppen i Gävle, tycker att det borde finnas regler för att marknadsföra hudvård till unga. – Just de här produkterna är milda och det är helt okej. Om man har besvär med med huden i tidig ålder bör man söka hjälp hos antingen auktoriserad hudterapeut eller läkare. Men det kan vara skadligt att använda aktiva ingredienser eller produkter i tidig ålder. Hon beskriver hur 10-åringar kommer till henne med påsar av produkter som de har testat. Och hur fler får kontaktallergi, vuxenakne, rosacea och perioral dermatit. – Det har ökat de senaste fem åren. Unga klickar hem vad som helst, säger hon.

articles.title: Svantesson sågar S: ”Provocerande”
articles.summary: Finansminister Elisabeth Svantesson (M) skickade en ordentlig känga till Magdalena Andersson (S) under onsdagens pressträff. Hon uppmanade S-delaren att tala ur skägget och sluta kritisera andra partier. – Det tycker jag är ansvarslöst och rätt provocerande, säger Svantesson.
articles.body_text: Finansminister Elisabeth Svantesson (M) skickade en ordentlig känga till Magdalena Andersson (S) under onsdagens pressträff. Hon uppmanade S-delaren att tala ur skägget och sluta kritisera andra partier. – Det tycker jag är ansvarslöst och rätt provocerande, säger Svantesson. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. På onsdagseftermiddagen kallade den moderata finansministern Elisabeth Svantesson till pressträff för att presentera det totalpaket som Moderaterna presenterat för Centerpartiet. – För mig är det högst relevant så klart att tala om detta därför att det ska finansieras, allt man gör behöver finansieras, säger Svantesson. Hon gick inte in på innehållet i totalpaketet, men gick däremot till attack mot det totalpaket som Socialdemokraterna presenterat för Centerpartiet. – Vad är då kostnaden för de här förslagen i det här totalpaketet? Det är 175 miljarder 2030. Siffran har Moderaterna kommit fram till genom att använda ”konventionella metoder”, säger hon till Expressen efter pressträffen. – Vi har framför allt tittat på partiernas egna beräkningar, deras budgetmotioner och när de har haft pressträffar, och i annat fall har vi utgått från de allmänna konventioner som gäller när man beräknar den här typen av förslag. Under pressträffen sa Svantesson att hon tror att paketet dessutom kommer att bli dyrare när fler partier ska vara involverade. – Jag kan också bara konstatera att det finns noll diskussion om finansiering, sa hon under pressträffen.

articles.title: Åkesson om granskningen: ”Tar det på allvar” | Expressen
articles.summary: Den 13 september går Sverige till val. Följ Expressens direktrapport med senaste nytt inför valet.
articles.body_text: SD-ledaren Jimmie Åkesson kommenterar nu Dagens Nyheters granskning av ungdomsförbundet Ungsvenskarna, där flera tidigare kvinnliga medlemmar vittnat om sexuella kränkningar. Bland annat pekas riksdagsledamoten Rasmus Giertz ut för att ha ofredat flera kvinnor i partiet. Giertz själv nekar till anklagelserna, och tar nu strid för sin riksdagsplats, trots att SD sagt att han ska avgå. – Jag har haft samtal med ungdomsförbundet kring det här och försäkrat mig om att de har rutiner på plats som behövs för att hantera den här typen av situationer och jag känner mig förvissad att man tar det på det allvar som det förtjänar, säger Jimmie Åkesson till journalister i riksdagen. Kommer han vara kvar i Sverigedemokraterna? – Jag kan inte svara på det. Det är andra som hanterar. Riksdagsledamot Jimmy Jansson (S) lämnar riksdagen. En avsägelse har kommit in till riksdagsförvaltningen. Jansson har tidigare lett Socialdemokraterna lokalt i Eskilstuna. I riksdagen valdes han in som suppleant i konstitutionsutskottet. I en skriftlig kommentar till Expressen säger Jansson att avhoppet handlar om personliga perspektiv och hans familj. ”Inte mycket att säga. Funderat noga på detta. Är väl genomtänkt. Handlar primärt om personliga perspektiv, familj och att inte vara offentlig och vad jag vill göra med livet framåt. Vad jag känner lust i. Vad jag fått smak på under året mellan förtroendeuppdrag.”, skriver Jimmy Jansson (S). Talmannen Andreas Norlén säger efter statsministeromröstningen att han kommer att samtala partiledarna under eftermiddagen. "Talman Andreas Norlén kommer under eftermiddagen den 15 oktober att diskutera med övriga partiledare om hur processen med regeringsbildningen ska fortskrida", står det i ett pressmeddelande från riksdagen. Under torsdagen röstades Magdalena Andersson (S) ner i den första statsministeromröstningen. Magdalena Andersson (S) blev nedröstad som statsminister. Ulf Kristersson (M) kallar det "påfallande svagt". – Magdalena Andersson har hittills misslyckats med att samla den rödgröna majoritet som efter valet sa att de ville se en ny regering. Det är inte förvånande, eftersom det kräver hårt arbete och gedigna förberedelser. Men det är ändå påfallande svagt.
